links.outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT NSCLC treatment recommendations versus NCCN guidelines, including hallucination rate
links.effect: GPT-4 base score 90% vs 60% for GPT-3.5; hallucinations 34% vs 53%; G-PS 0.34 vs -0.15 (P<.01).
links.quote: Analyzing 160 responses, generative pre-trained transformer (GPT)-4 outperformed GPT-3.5, showing higher base score (90% v 60%; P < .01) and fewer hallucinations (34% v 53%; P < .01).

links.outcome: Generative model performance on intended-use oncology treatment recommendations against NCCN guidelines
links.effect: GPT-4 hallucinated in 34% of responses and GPT-3.5 in 53%; GPT-4 G-PS 0.34, GPT-3.5 -0.15.
links.quote: Although the rate of hallucinations improved in the GPT-4 model, future generative AI use in clinical care requires high levels of accuracy with minimal to no room for hallucinations.

unlisted_practices: Composite generative AI performance score (G-PS) penalizing hallucinations to compare LLM recommendations to guidelines

screen.reason: Evaluates base performance of GPT-3.5 vs GPT-4 on clinical guideline adherence and hallucination rates for NSCLC treatment recommendations using a zero-shot benchmark, without testing a deployment safeguard or practice.
